canonical.name: The Turing reduction notion is stated in machine-language form as an oracle-decider model, because the directly verified sources mostly emphasize many-one reducibility and only contrast it informally with oracle reducibility.
Any many-one reduction yields a one-query oracle reduction by computing the target instance first and then asking the oracle once.
The strictness witness uses the complement of A_TM versus A_TM: the complement Turing-reduces to A_TM by one query but cannot many-one reduce back without becoming recognizable.
A_TM is lifted from generic r.e.-completeness to machine-acceptance completeness by the explicit map x ↦ <R,x> for a fixed recognizer R of the source language.
The standard semantic-property corollary is grouped as one item rather than exploded into separate emptiness, finiteness, regularity, and context-freedom leaves.
A valid many-one reduction preserves yes and no answers by an iff clause; reversing answers means changing the target to the complement.
State count is a code-level feature, not an extensional property of the recognized language.
The worked B-page transfer example uses the standard reduction from A_TM to nonemptiness to show how undecidability moves along a many-one reduction.
Adding an unreachable state changes syntax but not the recognized language.
The complement trick shows exactly why the slogan about reversing yes and no instances fails.

canonical.name: Boolean formulas, CNF, and the SAT language are localized here because the prerequisite page only used SAT inside a search-vs-decision theorem and did not mint this page's main definition item.
SAT is in NP by using a truth assignment as a polynomial-size certificate and evaluating the formula deterministically.
A bounded tableau is recorded explicitly as a rows-by-columns encoding of a polynomially bounded nondeterministic computation history.
For a fixed machine, the extended tableau alphabet is constant-size because cell contents come from a fixed tape symbol set plus at most one tagged state.
Exactly-one-symbol clauses have polynomial size because there are polynomially many cells and only constantly many symbol choices per cell.
The reduction map is polynomial-time because it writes only polynomially many variables and constant-width local clauses.
Tseitin extension variables name subformulas and avoid the exponential blowup of naive CNF distribution.
The Tseitin transformation is recorded as the linear-size equisatisfiable CNF route needed for the 3-SAT epilogue.
3-SAT is obtained by composing SAT completeness with the Tseitin conversion and short-clause padding.
A satisfying assignment encodes one accepting tableau, not an exhaustive list of all nondeterministic branches.
Naive full distribution to CNF can blow up exponentially; that is why the page keeps Tseitin as a separate lemma.
The fixed-machine alphabet count is illustrated on the B page by a concrete tableau encoding.
A small nested formula is converted to equisatisfiable 3-CNF as the B-page worked Tseitin example.
A machine with one accepting branch and one looping branch witnesses that Cook-Levin does not enumerate all branches.
